summary: Custom local facts come from files in /etc/ansible/facts.d (or a directory set with fact_path) ending in .fact. They can be JSON, INI or executable scripts returning JSON. Static fact files must not be executable. The results appear under ansible_local, namespaced by file name.
questions: How do I create static custom facts on a host with an INI file?
Where does Ansible look for local .fact files?
Can I change the facts.d directory location?
Why did my setup module break after adding a .fact file?
How do I check that my custom fact was picked up?
Under which variable do facts.d facts appear?

answer_card.title: Static custom facts with facts.d
answer_card.answer_md:
1. Create `/etc/ansible/facts.d` on the remote host (or another directory, set with the `fact_path` play keyword).
2. Add a file ending in `.fact`, for example `/etc/ansible/facts.d/preferences.fact`:

```ini
[general]
asdf=1
bar=2
```

The file can be JSON, INI or an executable returning JSON. A static file must **not** be executable, or `setup` breaks.

Check it:

```shell
ansible <hostname> -m ansible.builtin.setup -a "filter=ansible_local"
```

The data appears as `ansible_local.preferences.general`.
